missed_defects.evidence: First pass's step note claimed 'Bound-state energies themselves are robust to integrator noise' -- this is FALSE for the shallowest states. With the off-by-one cap held fixed, only default-tolerance odeint passes test 1: odeint default maxdiff 5.96e-8 (PASS, ~3x margin); odeint rtol=1e-10 maxdiff 2.10e-6 FAIL; LSODA rtol=1e-8 3.08e-6 FAIL; RK45 rtol=1e-8 2.49e-6 FAIL (steptest joint on the RK45 chain: FAIL). The failing entries are the shallowest (n=8-like) energies, e.g. target -0.01556687 vs RK45 -0.01556895, beyond elementwise tol ~1.7e-7. So even a solver who reproduces the nmax bug fails 52.4 unless they also guess 'odeint at default tolerances'.

summary: All 10 first-pass findings confirmed at their original severities, none refuted; 1 missed defect added (52.4 is also default-odeint-pinned -- the first pass wrongly asserted its energies were integrator-robust). The two blockers stand: 52.2 test 3 and 52.3 test 3 encode unconverged-integrator noise (52.3's converged truth even has the opposite sign) that no integrator setting reproduces, so both steps always fail in the current environment. The problem is fixable to fair with moderate effort: one method-pinning prompt_edit in 52.2 (rescues 52.2/52.3 tests 1-2 and 52.4), regen of the two noise targets (52.2/test3, 52.3/test3) on the pinned env -- or, more robustly, swap those tests to En<0 inputs -- plus a 52.1 test-input change with regen, the 52.4 nmax doc_edit, and three trivial doc/test edits.
